tasks.taskText: sinon.stub(obj, "prop").get(fn) and sinon.stub(obj, "prop").set(fn) install the replacement function directly as the property's accessor, so reading or writing the stubbed property runs the replacement untracked: nothing records the access and there is no call count to assert on. Wrap the replacement getter and the replacement setter in a spy and expose the spies on the stub as stub.getter and stub.setter, mirroring the spy.get and spy.set surface that sinon.spy(obj, "prop", ["get"]) produces. That surface is the whole sinon spy API, not a call counter: stub.getter and stub.setter must be sinon spies on which everything sinon.spy(fn) returns supports works the same way, among them callCount, calledOnce and calledThrice, calledWith, withArgs, getCall and firstCall, args, returnValues and resetHistory; a wrapper that only counts calls does not meet this. After const stub = sinon.stub(obj, "prop").get(() => "bar"), reading obj.prop three times must give "bar" each time and stub.getter.callCount must be 3 (stub.getter.calledThrice true); after const stub = sinon.stub(obj, "prop").set((value) => { obj.example = value }), assigning obj.prop = "bar" then obj.prop = "baz" must run the setter both times (obj.example is "baz") with stub.setter.callCount 2, stub.setter.calledWith("bar") true and stub.setter.withArgs("bar").callCount 1. stub.resetBehavior() must remove both, so stub.getter and stub.setter are undefined afterwards. Everything .get and .set do today must stay: the replacement runs, the property is defined configurable as before, restore works, and .get and .set stay chainable. Source is ESM under src/sinon/ (default-behaviors.js holds the get and set behaviours, stub.js the stub prototype, spy.js makes spies); the node tests run with npm run test-node (mocha over test/src, test/issues and test/scripts).

acorn's parser (acorn/src/expression.js) reports two errors in an object literal only once it knows the literal is not a destructuring pattern: a shorthand property with a default, as in {a = 0}, is "Shorthand property assignments are valid only in destructuring patterns", and a second __proto__ property is "Redefinition of __proto__ property". Today both errors are lost when the object literal is the object of a member expression that is itself an assignment target, although such a literal is never a pattern: with { ecmaVersion: 2022 }, parse("({a = 0}.x = 0);") succeeds, and so do parse("[{a = 0}.x] = [];"), parse("for ({a = 0}.x of []) ;") and parse("({__proto__: 1, __proto__: 2}.x = 0);"). Each must throw a SyntaxError: "({a = 0}.x = 0);" and "[{a = 0}.x] = [];" with "Shorthand property assignments are valid only in destructuring patterns (1:4)", "for ({a = 0}.x of []) ;" with the same message at (1:8), and "({__proto__: 1, __proto__: 2}.x = 0);" with "Redefinition of __proto__ property (1:16)". The same holds wherever such a literal is the object of a member expression that is assigned to or destructured into, however deep. What must not change: real destructuring patterns still parse ("({a = 0} = {});", "[{a = 0}] = [];", "({a = 0}) => 0;"), a member expression whose object has no such property still parses as a target ("[{a: 0}.x] = [];"), and the errors acorn reports today stay as they are ("({a = 0});" throws the shorthand message at (1:4); "({a = 0} += 1);" throws "Assigning to rvalue (1:1)"). The parser's source is in acorn/src; npm test builds it and runs the test files under test/ (the parser's expression tests are in test/tests-harmony.js, written with test() and testFail()). Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm test.

entities no longer exports getCodePoint from src/escape.ts, a helper its earlier releases exported and code that depends on the package still imports from the escape module; today importing it gives undefined. Restore it in src/escape.ts as a deprecated export (marked @deprecated in favour of String.prototype.codePointAt): getCodePoint(input, index) returns the Unicode code point that starts at index in input, reading a surrogate pair as one astral code point, and NaN where index is outside the string. getCodePoint("abc", 0) must give 97, getCodePoint("abc", 2) 99, getCodePoint("ü", 0) 252, getCodePoint("💯", 0) 128175, getCodePoint("a💩", 1) 128169, and getCodePoint("abc", 3) and getCodePoint("", 0) NaN. What must not change: the other exports of src/escape.ts and their results (encodeXML(`'&' 💯 ü`) gives "<a href="x">'&'</a> 💯 ü" and escapeUTF8 of the same string gives "<a href="x">'&'</a> 💯 ü"), and the exports of src/index.ts, which do not include getCodePoint. The source is TypeScript in src/, with its vitest tests beside it (src/escape.spec.ts tests the escape module). Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm run test:vi.
